CollaboratoR Example

collaborator_example.Rmd
library(CollaboratoR)

Overview

This walks through an example of a collection of example Google Sheets needed for collaborative data entry, how to configure the software (the pieces of infromation you need), and how to automatically download and validate the data.

Example Data

This walk-through will use a small collection of short files from what’s known as “Fisher’s Iris data” or “Anderson’s Iris data”: a famous data set of measurments of flower sepals and petals collected by Edgar Anderson on the Gaspé Peninsula in Quebec (Anderson 1936).

As of this writing, there is a public folder in Google Docs/Workspace with these files

If this is no longer available (nothing is forever!), in the raw_data folder of this repository](https://github.com/IBEEM-MSU/CollaboratoR) is a zip file containing XLSX formatted versions of these sheets that you may upload to your own Google Drive shared folder (full instructions for recreating our examle data set in Google drive is TBD)

While this data set is small, they are split by species in the sheets to simulate collaborative data.

Getting started: setting up data sheets for entry

This package was designed to assist with a workflow that used spreadsheets for the following functions. After designing the goals and basic process/protocol for your study, to use spreadshseets to collect data and use this package, one should include the following types of sheets in the table below:

Element Description/Function example sheet names example sheet description
data entry protocol (distinct from the data collection protocol, this is a detailed description how
data extract from field data or for a meta analysis, not specific to this package		 Iris data entry protocol ficitious protocol for how measurements may be collaboratively entered for validation
data specification list of variables included in data entry sheets with data types, i.e. the ‘data dictionary.’ All variables here should be represented
in the data entry template		 measurements_spec List of Sepal and petal measurements with grouping and entry information
data sheet template this is not required but helpful. a blank spreadsheet with columns as defined in the
data specification.		 iris_template example blank data sheet, to be copied and saved for per-species data entry
data sheets copies of template filled with data, each row identifies who entered these data, and data/tasks is split on a logical grouping depending on your protocol/process. iris_setosa, iris_versicolor, iris_virginica per-species sepal and petal measurment data for this example
data sheet list a table of all data sheets ready for validation with URLs for CollaboratoR to read from id_urls listing of data sheets above with Google Sheets URLs
group lookup values columns holding identifying variables used groupming must be entered correctly. A list of the acceptable values for that grouping variable is useful for both the data entry template and for the validation step. An example categorical grouping column may be “species” (as in our example). CollaboratoR currently can only provide this function for one column. species a single column list of species included in this example project, used for both validation steps, and for limiting data in the data entry template spreadsheet

saved…

The folder for this example project has the following sheets in it

  • Iris data entry protocol: ficitious protocol for how measurements may be collaboratively entered for validation.
  • id_urls : table of data sheets and their associated google urls
  • iris_template : example blank data sheet to use for new entries
  • iris_setosa, iris_versicolor, iris_virginica : data sheets by species
  • measurements_spec : the ‘data dictionary’ list of variables in data sheets with descriptions
  • species : a single column list of species included in this data project, used for both validation steps, and for limiting data in the data entry template spreadsheet

saved… Process: Getting Started

After designing the goals and basic process/protocol for your study, to use spreadshseets to collect data and use this package, one should include the following:

  • data entry protocol (distinct from the data collection protocol)
  • data specification: list of variables included in data entry sheets
  • template data sheet, a blank spreadsheet with columns as defined in the data specification
  • One or more data sheets, creatd from the template
  • a table of all data sheets ready for validation

The example sheets above ## Process: CollaboratoR Set

  • installing this package and it’s dependencies (Readr, etc)

Setup/Configuration

  • Install using instructions in the project’s README
  • Information on how to set-up google workspace in the vignette for Google Sheets API setup.
  • This package relies on configuration values in the .Renviron file

Workflow Summary

  1. Write your data entry protocol (outside of this system but crucial for organization)
  2. Setup Git repositories to hold data as it flows through
  3. Create metadata and configuration
  • column definintions for main data sheet (CSV or Googlesheets)
  • create validation rules (YAML format)
  • data lists such as species lists in CSV or
  • list/table for tracking data entry sheets
  • CollaboratoR configuration in .Renviron
  1. Enter data into tabular form
  • CSV or GoogleSheets
  • add entry to list of URIs (Google sheet urls or CSV file paths)
  1. Use CollaboratoR package to accumulate metadata
  • read metadata: column specification, list of data sheet URIs
  • reads in list of data sheets CSV filename or list of googlesheets URLs
  • validation rules written in YAML and stored a RData file
  1. automated validation and report
  • read data files (from list of URIs in CSV or Google Sheets)
  • data format against schema (from column spec)
  • category columns are checked against lists (i.e. species lists)
  • data values against rules (from YAML file)
  • report errors printed for user
  1. save to git
  • those sheets that passed validation are commited to git
  1. combine to master list(s)
  • a master database

Workflow

Write your data entry protocol

This is beyond the scope of this documentation and package, but crucial for successful data synthesis projects. The process for finding, extracting and formatting every data point is crucial. This protocol will the determine the columns in the datsheet and column definitions in metadata

Create metadata and configuration

Create a table describing the columns in the each to data files based on the protocol. This table must have columns as follows:

Column Description
col_name exact name of column as it will appear in the datasheet
col_description human reable description based on your data collection protocol
col_type name of the datatype, see datatype list below
example human readable example for guidance 
col_name,col_description,col_type,example
id,"id formed from species group and sample location", character,"SetosaMBG"
Sepal.L., "Sepal length (mm)", double,5.1
Sepal.W., "Sepal width (mm)", double,3.5
Petal.L., "Petal length (mm)", double,1.4
Petal.W., "Petal width (mm)", double,0.2
group_id, "grouping variable", factor, "SetosaMBG"
whos, "collector of measurements", character, "ESA"
site, "name of the site where the data was collected", character, "Main Site"
  • create validation rules (YAML format)
  • data lists such as species lists in CSV or
  • list/table for tracking data entry sheets
  • CollaboratoR configuration in .Renviron

Enter data into tabular form

  • CSV or GoogleSheets
  • add entry to list of URIs (Google sheet urls or CSV file paths)

Use CollaboratoR package to accumulate metadata

  • read metadata: column specification, list of data sheet URIs
  • reads in list of data sheets CSV filename or list of googlesheets URLs
  • validation rules written in YAML and stored a RData file

Initiate automated validation and report

  • read data files (from list of URIs in CSV or Google Sheets)
  • data format against schema (from column spec)
  • category columns are checked against lists (i.e. species lists)
  • data values against rules (from YAML file)
  • report errors printed for user ## save to git
  • those sheets that passed validation are committed to git
